templates.title: AFFiNE
templates.description: Workspace combining documents, whiteboards, collections and collaborative knowledge management. Includes private PostgreSQL with the required pgvector extension, Redis, persistent storage/configuration and one-time database migration. Plain PostgreSQL lacks the vector extension required by the application schema.
templates.name: affine
templates.note: Set AFFINE_URL and POSTGRES_PASSWORD before deployment. A configuration job writes server.externalUrl to persistent config.json; the upstream migration job initializes the database and generates private.key once. Open port 3010 on a trusted network and complete the first-run administrator wizard. Preserve the entire config volume, especially private.key, plus uploaded storage and PostgreSQL. This stack uses pgvector on PostgreSQL 18 because the ordinary catalog PostgreSQL image has no vector extension. Indexer, SMTP, AI and external storage can be configured separately. Use HTTPS for remote access. Documentation: https://docs.affine.pro/self-host-affine/install/docker-compose-recommended

New Appwrite 2.6.2 installation. Set the hostname and separate private database, encryption and service secrets. Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ and Docker socket access for runtime services.

This PostgreSQL template does not migrate Appwrite 1.1.1/MariaDB data. Preserve existing keys and follow the upstream upgrade procedure.

Setup and migration guide

env.name: COUCH_DB_USER
env.label: CouchDB username
env.description: Required. CouchDB account shared by the app, worker and database initialization services. This value is interpolated into a URL; use URL-safe characters.

env.name: COUCH_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: CouchDB password
env.description: Required. Set a private CouchDB password shared by the app, worker and initialization services. This value is interpolated into a URL; use URL-safe characters and retain existing database credentials on updates.

env.name: MINIO_ACCESS_KEY
env.label: MinIO access key
env.description: Required. Set the MinIO account identifier shared by the app, worker and object storage service. Retain the account used by existing storage on updates.

env.name: MINIO_SECRET_KEY
env.label: MinIO secret key
env.description: Required. Set a private MinIO secret shared by the app, worker and object storage service. Retain the secret used by existing storage on updates.

env.name: INTERNAL_API_KEY
env.label: Internal API key
env.description: Required. Generate a private internal API key, for example with openssl rand -hex 32. The app and worker share this value; keep it across updates.

env.name: BUDIBASE_ENVIRONMENT
env.label: Budibase environment
env.description: Set the runtime environment value required by the deployed Budibase release, using that release's self-hosting configuration. This stack provides no default.

env.name: JWT_SECRET
env.label: JWT signing secret
env.description: Required. Generate a private signing secret, for example with openssl rand -hex 32. The app and worker share it; retain it across updates.

env.name: REDIS_PASSWORD
env.label: Redis password
env.description: Required. Set a private Redis password shared by Redis, the app and worker. Use a value without whitespace because this stack inserts it into the Redis command.

env.name: PLUGINS_DIR

env.description: Set the absolute plugins directory inside the app container. The supplied stack mounts its host plugins directory at /plugins; use that container path when keeping the supplied mount.

env.name: MAIN_PORT
env.label: Host web port

templates.note: Set BASE_URL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, SECRET_KEY, BUGSINK_ADMIN_EMAIL and BUGSINK_ADMIN_PASSWORD before deployment. The database password must be URL-safe: generate with openssl rand -hex 32. SECRET_KEY must be at least 50 characters; openssl rand -hex 32 provides 64. Open port 8000, sign in with the configured initial administrator and create a project to obtain its SDK DSN. Set BEHIND_HTTPS_PROXY true only behind a trusted HTTPS proxy. Email defaults to console logging. Preserve the database and signing secret. Documentation: https://www.bugsink.com/docs/postgresql/

env.name: BUGSINK_ADMIN_PASSWORD

templates.title: Cops
templates.description: Cops by Sébastien Lucas, now maintained by MikesPub, stands for Calibre OPDS (and HTML) Php Server. COPS links to your Calibre library database and allows downloading and emailing of books directly from a web browser and provides a OPDS feed to connect to your devices. Changes in your Calibre library are reflected immediately in your COPS pages. See : COPS's home for more details. Don't forget to check the Wiki. ## Why? (taken from the author's site) In my opinion Calibre is a marvelous tool but is too big and has too much dependencies to be used for its content server. That's the main reason why I coded this OPDS server. I needed a simple tool to be installed on a small server (Seagate Dockstar in my case). I initially thought of Calibre2OPDS but as it generate static file no search was possible. Later I added an simple HTML catalog that should be usable on my Kobo. So COPS's main advantages are : * No need for many dependencies. * No need for a lot of CPU or RAM. * Not much code. * Search is available. * With Dropbox / owncloud it's very easy to have an up to date OPDS server. * It was fun to code. If you want to use the OPDS feed don't forget to specify /feed at the end of your URL.
templates.name: cops

templates.title: Windows (dockur)
templates.description: Runs a full Windows installation inside a Docker container, with automatic hands-free download and setup. Supports Windows 11 down to 95, plus several Windows Server releases, via near-native KVM acceleration. Access it through the built-in web viewer on port 8006 during setup, then over RDP afterwards. NOTE - requires a Linux host with KVM support (not available under Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows, or most container-only cloud hosts). It also needs the NET_ADMIN capability plus /dev/kvm and /dev/net/tun device access; since Portainer's template format can't grant just those, this deploys in --privileged mode instead (full access to the host's devices and capabilities) - a much bigger grant than the container actually needs, so prefer a host you trust before deploying.

Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image with its own database and volume.

templates.note: Requires an AMD64 Docker host, or configured AMD64 emulation on ARM. Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DOCSPELL_ADMIN_SECRET, DOCSPELL_AUTH_SECRET and DOCSPELL_INVITE_PASSWORD before deployment. templates.title: Documenso
templates.description: Prepare, send and track documents for electronic signing. Includes a private PostgreSQL database and stores uploaded documents in the database. Requires your own PKCS#12 signing certificate and working outgoing email. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image in a separate database instance and volume.

templates.note: Set NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, both encryption keys, SMTP credentials and DOCUMENSO_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_SECRET. The certificate value is the single-line Base64 of YOUR encrypted .p12 certificate, including its private key; set its password in DOCUMENSO_SIGNING_PASSWORD. Generate or obtain the certificate locally using the upstream signing-certificate guide before deployment. No sample certificate is provided. Open port 3016 on a trusted network, create the first account and configure signup restrictions. Documents use database storage. Back up PostgreSQL, the certificate and all keys together; SMTP is needed for email delivery. Use HTTPS for signing links. templates.title: Ente Photos
templates.description: End-to-end encrypted photo and video library with mobile backup, shared albums and web clients. Includes the Ente API, Photos, Albums and Accounts interfaces, private PostgreSQL and a persistent S3-compatible Silo object store. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image with its own database and volume.
templates.name: ente-photos
templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for inline configuration. Set all public URLs, ENTE_S3_ENDPOINT and the required secrets before deploying. Museum and every client must reach S3 at the same endpoint; do not use localhost or an internal Docker hostname. The bundled S3 service is exposed on ENTE_S3_PORT. Put Photos, Albums, Accounts, API and S3 behind HTTPS reverse proxies, or set ENTE_S3_USE_HTTP=true for a trusted HTTP-only LAN. Account verification codes are logged until SMTP is configured. The first account is the instance administrator; self-hosted accounts are separate from Ente Cloud. Back up PostgreSQL, S3 data and all encryption keys together. Keep all keys on updates; losing them can make stored data unusable. Replication is disabled. Documentation: https://ente.com/help/self-hosting/

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it and the database volume on updates. Use hexadecimal characters because some stacks embed it in connection URLs or YAML.

env.name: ENTE_PHOTOS_URL
env.label: Photos URL
env.description: Required. External Photos origin, such as https://photos.example.com. No trailing slash.

env.name: ENTE_ALBUMS_URL
env.label: Public albums URL
env.description: Required. External Albums origin, such as https://albums.example.com. No trailing slash.

env.name: ENTE_ACCOUNTS_URL
env.label: Accounts URL
env.description: Required. External Accounts origin, such as https://accounts.example.com. No trailing slash.

env.name: ENTE_API_URL
env.label: API URL
env.description: Required. Ente API origin reachable from browsers and mobile devices, such as https://api.photos.example.com.

env.name: ENTE_S3_ENDPOINT
env.label: Public S3 endpoint
env.description: Required. Full S3 origin reachable at the SAME address from Museum and all clients, for example https://s3.photos.example.com. Route it to the bundled S3 port.

env.name: ENTE_S3_USE_HTTP
env.label: Use unencrypted S3 HTTP
env.description: Keep false for HTTPS. Set true only when ENTE_S3_ENDPOINT uses http:// on a trusted LAN.

env.name: ENTE_S3_ACCESS_KEY
env.label: S3 access key
env.description: Required. Generate a unique alphanumeric access key with openssl rand -hex 16; preserve it on updates.

env.name: ENTE_S3_SECRET_KEY
env.label: S3 secret key
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32; preserve it on updates.

env.name: ENTE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
env.label: Server encryption key
env.description: Required. Exactly 32 random bytes encoded as Base64: openssl rand -base64 32. Preserve it permanently.

env.name: ENTE_HASH_KEY
env.label: Server hash key
env.description: Required. Exactly 64 random bytes encoded as one Base64 line: openssl rand -base64 64 | tr -d "\n". Preserve it permanently.

env.name: ENTE_JWT_SECRET
env.label: Session signing secret
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it on updates.

env.name: ENTE_WEB_PORT
env.label: Photos web port
env.description: Free host TCP port for Photos, from 1 to 65535.

env.name: ENTE_ALBUMS_PORT
env.label: Albums web port
env.description: Free host TCP port for public albums, distinct from the other Ente ports.

env.name: ENTE_ACCOUNTS_PORT
env.label: Accounts web port
env.description: Free host TCP port for account flows, distinct from the other Ente ports.

env.name: ENTE_API_PORT
env.label: API port
env.description: Free host TCP port for the Ente API, distinct from the other Ente ports.

env.name: ENTE_S3_PORT
env.label: S3 API port
env.description: Free host TCP port for object uploads. Match the address or reverse proxy used in ENTE_S3_ENDPOINT.

templates.title: Formbricks
templates.description: Survey and feedback platform with a form builder, link surveys and analytics. Includes PostgreSQL with pgvector, Valkey, SpiceDB authorization, Hub API/background processing, Cube analytics and their initialization jobs. Uses a pgvector PostgreSQL 18 image because the ordinary PostgreSQL catalog image lacks the required extension.

templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for inline scripts and analytics configuration. Set FORMBRICKS_URL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, AUTHZED_DATABASE_PASSWORD, REDIS_PASSWORD and all application/service secrets before deployment. Generate URL-safe database/cache passwords and 64-character hexadecimal encryption/authentication keys with openssl rand -hex 32. Wait for migrations, authorization initialization and analytics health checks, then open host port 3017 on a trusted network and create the first account/organization. Email verification and password reset are disabled until SMTP is configured. Review signup restrictions after onboarding. Back up the database, cache and upload/SAML volumes; retain all secrets. Use HTTPS for public survey links. This stack deploys the open-source feature set; enterprise and optional AI services need separate configuration. Embedded upstream scripts/models retain their license in stacks/formbricks/LICENSE.upstream. Documentation: https://formbricks.com/docs/self-hosting/deployment

templates.description: Encrypted, deduplicated backups with snapshot schedules, retention policies and a web repository manager. The source directory /srv/dockyard/kopia/source is mounted read-only from the host. Uses persistent configuration, cache, logs and a local repository volume; no privileged mode or FUSE mount is enabled.

templates.note: Set KOPIA_PASSWORD and a different KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD before deployment. Open port 51515 on a trusted network and sign in with KOPIA_SERVER_USERNAME. Put files to back up under /srv/dockyard/kopia/source, or edit that read-only bind to the intended source. For off-host protection choose remote storage in the UI. Preserve the repository password and configuration; a local repository volume alone does not survive host loss. Restore to a separate writable target or download through the UI. templates.name: netbird
templates.note: Requires a public Linux server, DNS pointing NETBIRD_DOMAIN to it, free TCP 80/443 and UDP 3478, and Docker Compose 2.23.1+. NETBIRD_DOMAIN is a plain DNS hostname without scheme, path, quotes or whitespace. Generate the relay secret with openssl rand -hex 32; generate the two encryption keys separately with openssl rand -base64 32. Preserve all keys and volumes. Visit https://NETBIRD_DOMAIN/setup to create the first administrator, then install NetBird clients. The private bridge uses 172.30.0.0/24; adjust it if your networks overlap. Documentation: https://docs.netbird.io/selfhosted/selfhosted-quickstart

env.name: NETBIRD_DOMAIN
env.label: Public DNS hostname
env.description: Required. Plain hostname such as netbird.example.com, without scheme, path, quotes or whitespace.

env.name: LETSENCRYPT_EMAIL
env.label: Certificate email
env.description: Required. Plain email address for Caddy certificate registration; no quotes or whitespace.

env.name: NETBIRD_RELAY_AUTH_SECRET
env.label: Relay authentication secret
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32; retain it on updates.

env.name: NETBIRD_DATASTORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
env.label: Data encryption key

templates.title: Plane
templates.description: Plane 1.4.2 Community Edition project management with prebuilt web, API, worker and realtime images, PostgreSQL, Valkey and RabbitMQ. Includes RustFS 1.0.4 object storage and automatic bucket creation. Set the public URL and private database, queue, storage and application secrets. No source build, separate configuration files or external S3 account are needed. Put the HTTP proxy behind HTTPS. This creates a new installation; use the upstream migration procedure for existing Plane data. See stacks/plane/README.md.
templates.name: plane
templates.note:
Plane 1.4.2 with private RustFS 1.0.4 storage. Supply the public URL and separate database, queue, application, realtime and storage secrets. The uploads bucket is created automatically. Put the HTTP listener behind your HTTPS reverse proxy.

This creates a new installation; existing databases and MinIO object data require a reviewed migration.

Setup and storage guide

env.name: PLANE_DOMAIN
env.label: Public hostname
env.description: Required. Hostname without scheme or path, for example plane.example.com. It must match WEB_URL and your HTTPS reverse proxy.

env.name: WEB_URL
env.label: Public URL
env.description: Required. Full external URL, for example https://plane.example.com. Used for links and allowed browser origins; it must match the actual browser address.

env.name: PGUSER
env.label: Database username
env.description: PostgreSQL role shared by every backend service. Use letters, digits and underscores because it is included in the database URL.

env.name: PGDATABASE
env.label: Database name
env.description: PostgreSQL database shared by every backend service. Use letters, digits and underscores.

env.name: PGPASSWORD
env.label: Database password
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32; use hexadecimal characters because this value is inserted into DATABASE_URL. Keep the password of an existing database on updates.

env.name: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
env.label: Queue password
env.description: Required. Generate a separate value with openssl rand -hex 32. Use hexadecimal characters because this value is inserted into AMQP_URL.

env.name: PLANE_SECRET_KEY
env.label: Application secret
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32 and retain it across updates. Do not reuse the database or queue password.

env.name: LIVE_SERVER_SECRET_KEY
env.label: Realtime secret
env.description: Required. Generate a separate value with openssl rand -hex 32. API, workers and the live service use the same value.

env.name: AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME
env.label: Uploads bucket
env.description: Bucket created automatically in bundled RustFS. Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; retain the name when reusing storage.

env.name: AWS_REGION
env.label: Storage region
env.description: Signing region for the bundled RustFS service. Keep us-east-1 for this local setup.

env.name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.label: RustFS access key
env.description: Required. Private account identifier for bundled RustFS and Plane. Use at least 3 URL-safe characters; do not use the public rustfsadmin example.

env.name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
env.label: RustFS secret key
env.description: Required private RustFS password of at least 8 characters, paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID. The same value is shared with Plane and bucket initialization; retain it when reusing storage.

env.name: PLANE_PORT
env.label: Host HTTP port
env.description: Free host TCP port for the bundled proxy. Route the public HTTPS URL to this port; TLS is terminated by your external reverse proxy.

env.name: FILE_SIZE_LIMIT
env.label: Upload size limit
env.description: Maximum proxy upload size in bytes, for example 5242880 for 5 MiB. Match any limits enforced by the external reverse proxy and storage provider.

templates.description: Self-hosted Community Edition of Plausible web analytics, with traffic sources, page views, goals and a lightweight website tracking script. Includes private PostgreSQL and ClickHouse databases. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image with a separate database and volume.
templates.name: plausible
templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for inline ClickHouse configuration. Set BASE_URL to the external HTTPS URL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, SECRET_KEY_BASE and TOTP_VAULT_KEY. Generate URL-safe database passwords with openssl rand -hex 32. SECRET_KEY_BASE needs at least 64 characters; TOTP_VAULT_KEY is 32 random bytes in Base64. Open the web interface on a trusted network to create the first administrator, add a website and install its tracking script. Registration is invite-only after initial setup. Use an existing HTTPS reverse proxy. SMTP is optional for invitations, password resets and reports. Back up both databases and keep the signing and TOTP keys. Documentation: https://github.com/plausible/community-edition

Personal use allows one registered account; additional registered users require a paid self-hosting license. Guest voters do not count toward the user limit.

templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for inline Garage configuration. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL, RALLLY_ADMIN_EMAIL, the database, session and Garage secrets, and working SMTP credentials. Login uses email verification, so SMTP must work before onboarding. The admin email is also the allowed-account list in this template; guest voting remains available. Open the configured URL and sign in with that email. SECRET_PASSWORD must have at least 32 characters. GARAGE_RPC_SECRET and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are 32 random bytes in hexadecimal; S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID is 16 random bytes in hexadecimal. Preserve all credentials and PostgreSQL/Garage volumes on updates. This stack uses the existing pinned PostgreSQL image in its own instance. Licensing: https://support.rallly.co/self-hosting/licensing Documentation: https://support.rallly.co/self-hosting/

env.name: APP_URL
env.label: Public application URL
env.description: Required for a normal deployment. Full external URL, for example https://time.example.com. Use the same URL in your reverse proxy and email configuration.

env.name: APP_KEY
env.label: Application encryption key
env.description: Required. Use the APP_KEY value from php artisan self-host:generate-keys in the deployed Solidtime release, including its base64: prefix. Paste the value without the assignment or surrounding quotes and keep it across updates.

env.name: DB_PASSWORD
env.label: PostgreSQL password
env.description: Required. Set a private password shared by Solidtime, its workers and PostgreSQL. Keep the password already used by an existing database.

env.name: SUPER_ADMINS
env.label: Super-administrator emails
env.description: Comma-separated email addresses allowed super-administrator access, for example admin@example.com,owner@example.com, without spaces between entries. This grants privileges to matching verified accounts; it does not create accounts or enable registration. Leave empty when no super-administrator access is needed.

env.name: MAIL_HOST
env.label: SMTP server hostname
env.description: Required when using SMTP delivery. Server hostname without a scheme, for example smtp.example.com. This stack uses the smtp mailer unless overridden and defaults its port to 587.

env.name: MAIL_USERNAME
env.label: SMTP username
env.description: Set the username when your SMTP server requires authentication. Leave empty only when the configured mail server permits unauthenticated delivery from this deployment.

env.name: MAIL_PASSWORD
env.label: SMTP password
env.description: Set the private password or app password when your SMTP server requires authentication. Use together with MAIL_USERNAME; leave empty only for an authorized relay that needs no authentication.

env.name: PASSPORT_PRIVATE_KEY
env.label: OAuth private key
env.description: Use the PASSPORT_PRIVATE_KEY value from php artisan self-host:generate-keys in the deployed Solidtime release. Paste the PEM value without the assignment or surrounding quotes, preserving its generated newline escapes. Keep this private key paired with PASSPORT_PUBLIC_KEY across updates.

env.name: PASSPORT_PUBLIC_KEY
env.label: OAuth public key
env.description: Use the PASSPORT_PUBLIC_KEY value paired with PASSPORT_PRIVATE_KEY from php artisan self-host:generate-keys. Paste the PEM value without the assignment or surrounding quotes, preserving its generated newline escapes. Supply key content rather than a host file path.

env.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.label: S3 access key (optional)
env.description: Set when enabling S3-compatible storage. Account identifier for the chosen storage service; leave empty when using local storage. This stack does not select an S3 storage disk automatically.

env.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
env.label: S3 secret key (optional)
env.description: Set the private storage secret when enabling S3-compatible storage. Use together with S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_BUCKET and S3_ENDPOINT; leave empty when using local storage.

env.name: S3_BUCKET
env.label: S3 bucket (optional)
env.description: Existing bucket name when enabling S3-compatible storage, for example solidtime-uploads. Provision its access separately; leave empty when using local storage.

env.name: S3_ENDPOINT
env.label: S3 endpoint URL (optional)
env.description: Endpoint URL required by your S3-compatible provider, for example https://s3.example.com. Leave empty when using local storage or when the configured provider uses its standard endpoint. Configure storage disk selection separately.

templates.title: Synapse (Matrix)
templates.description: Matrix homeserver for self-hosted messaging and federation, used with clients such as Element. Includes private PostgreSQL and persistent media/signing keys. Automatically generates initial server keys; public registration is disabled. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image with a separate database and volume.
templates.name: synapse
templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for inline configuration. Choose SYNAPSE_SERVER_NAME permanently before first use; it forms Matrix user IDs and cannot be changed later. Set SYNAPSE_PUBLIC_BASEURL, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and the three application secrets. The init service generates signing keys in the persistent data volume. HTTP binds to localhost by default. For a remote proxy, set SYNAPSE_BIND_IP to a trusted interface and restrict the port to that proxy. Serve /_matrix and /_synapse/client through an HTTPS reverse proxy to port 8008 and configure federation delegation/.well-known records as described upstream. Create an administrator locally with docker compose exec synapse register_new_matrix_user -c /etc/synapse/homeserver.yaml http://localhost:8008, then connect a Matrix client. Back up PostgreSQL and the entire data volume, including the signing key, and retain all secrets. A browser client and TURN server are separate services. Documentation: https://element-hq.github.io/synapse/latest/setup/installation.html

env.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it and the database volume on updates. Use hexadecimal characters because some stacks embed it in connection URLs or YAML.

env.name: SYNAPSE_SERVER_NAME
env.label: Permanent Matrix server name
env.description: Required. DNS name used in Matrix IDs, for example matrix.example.com. No scheme, path or trailing slash. Cannot be changed after first use.

env.name: SYNAPSE_PUBLIC_BASEURL
env.label: Public server URL
env.description: Required. Full external HTTPS URL, for example https://matrix.example.com/.

env.name: SYNAPSE_REGISTRATION_SHARED_SECRET
env.label: Local account creation secret
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. Used by register_new_matrix_user while public signup remains disabled.

env.name: SYNAPSE_MACAROON_SECRET_KEY
env.label: Session signing secret
env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32; preserve it on updates.

env.name: SYNAPSE_FORM_SECRET
env.label: Form signing secret
env.description: Required. Generate a different value with openssl rand -hex 32 and keep it on updates.

env.name: SYNAPSE_PORT
env.label: HTTP reverse proxy port
env.description: Free host TCP port for the internal HTTP listener. Terminate public HTTPS at your reverse proxy.

env.name: SYNAPSE_BIND_IP
env.label: HTTP bind address
env.description: Keep 127.0.0.1 for a reverse proxy on this host. For a remote proxy, choose a trusted interface address and restrict port access to that proxy because forwarded headers are trusted.

templates.title: Tinyauth
templates.description: Authentication gateway for an existing reverse proxy, with local users, optional TOTP, OAuth, LDAP and OpenID Connect. Uses SQLite and persistent local keys. Proxy routing and forward-auth rules must be configured separately for each protected application.
templates.name: tinyauth
templates.note: Set TINYAUTH_APPURL to an HTTPS authentication hostname and TINYAUTH_AUTH_TRUSTEDPROXIES to the exact proxy IPs/CIDRs. Place Tinyauth and protected apps on sibling subdomains of the same parent domain. Create a user locally with docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/tinyauthapp/tinyauth:v5.2.0 user create --interactive, then set TINYAUTH_AUTH_USERS to the raw username:bcrypt-hash string. Treat that value as a secret. In Portainer/MCP environment inputs use ordinary dollar signs; double them only when embedding the hash directly in Compose YAML. Connect the proxy to port 3000 and configure its forward-auth endpoint, such as /api/auth/traefik. Back up /data. OIDC clients and external providers need their own configuration. Documentation: https://tinyauth.app/docs/getting-started/

env.name: TINYAUTH_AUTH_USERS

env.description: Required secret. Comma-separated username:bcrypt-hash entries from the Tinyauth user create command. Paste raw hashes into environment inputs.

env.name: TINYAUTH_AUTH_TRUSTEDPROXIES

env.description: Required. Comma-separated IPs or CIDRs of your actual reverse proxy; do not trust arbitrary clients.

env.name: TINYAUTH_AUTH_SECURECOOKIE
env.label: HTTPS session cookies
env.description: Keep true when using the required HTTPS reverse proxy.

env.label: OIDC private key path

env.name: TINYAUTH_OIDC_PUBLICKEYPATH
env.label: OIDC public key path
env.description: Path to the persistent public key file.

env.name: TINYAUTH_RESOURCES_PATH
env.label: Resources directory

templates.title: Windmill
templates.description: Code-based automation platform that turns scripts into workflows, forms, APIs and internal tools. Includes a server, standard worker, native worker and private PostgreSQL. The standard worker runs privileged for namespace isolation, granting broad access to the host; execute only trusted code. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image in a separate database instance and volume.
templates.name: windmill
templates.note: Requires a Linux Docker host and separate privileged-access approval in MCP. The standard worker follows the upstream privileged namespace-isolation setup. Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, then access the web UI through localhost or your HTTPS reverse proxy. The initial upstream administrator is admin@windmill.dev with password changeme; change it immediately before sharing access, then configure the instance base URL. HTTP binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. If using a remote proxy, choose a trusted WINDMILL_BIND_IP and restrict port access. Back up PostgreSQL, worker logs and dependency cache. This template does not include LSP/multiplayer extras or expose a Docker socket to scripts. Documentation: https://www.windmill.dev/docs/advanced/self_host

env.description: Required. Generate with openssl rand -hex 32. Use URL-safe hexadecimal characters because connection URLs embed this password. Retain it and the database volume on updates.

env.name: WINDMILL_BIND_IP

env.description: Keep 127.0.0.1 for initial setup or a local reverse proxy. Only change to an interface protected by your access controls.

templates.title: Wireguard
templates.description: WireGuard® is an extremely simple yet fast and modern VPN that utilizes state-of-the-art cryptography. It aims to be faster, simpler, leaner, and more useful than IPsec, while avoiding the massive headache. It intends to be considerably more performant than OpenVPN. WireGuard is designed as a general purpose VPN for running on embedded interfaces and super computers alike, fit for many different circumstances. Initially released for the Linux kernel, it is now cross-platform (Windows, macOS, BSD, iOS, Android) and widely deployable. It is currently under heavy development, but already it might be regarded as the most secure, easiest to use, and simplest VPN solution in the industry.

templates.title: Zammad
templates.description: Helpdesk for customer conversations, email tickets, teams and support workflows. Includes application initialization, web/API, scheduler, WebSockets, local backup jobs, private PostgreSQL, Redis, Memcached and Elasticsearch. Reuses the pinned PostgreSQL catalog image in a separate database instance and volume.
templates.name: zammad
templates.note: Requires Docker Compose 2.23.1+ for the inline PostgreSQL initialization script. Set ZAMMAD_HOSTNAME, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, a different POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD and REDIS_PASSWORD. Prepare the Docker host for Elasticsearch using its upstream virtual-memory requirements; the configured Elasticsearch JVM heap is 1 GiB. This stack provisions a dedicated non-superuser Zammad database role. Wait for initialization, open host port 8087 through your HTTPS reverse proxy and complete the first-administrator wizard. Forward WebSockets. Configure incoming/outgoing mail in the app. Back up PostgreSQL, application storage, search data and local backups; local backup jobs do not replace off-host backups. Initial database credentials apply to fresh volumes only. Documentation: https://docs.zammad.org/en/latest/install/docker-compose.html
